source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Obtain and review all inspection records related to the water-quality tests that failed. Make sure you have documentation of the specific test(s) conducted, the exact dates and times, the parameters tested, the laboratory results, and the narrative of what inspectors observed during the testing.

3. Verify the compliance thresholds.
Identify the specific thresholds that the water failed to meet, ensuring you understand the legal and public health standards in question. These thresholds will be outlined in local, state, or federal regulations, such as those specified by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in the United States.

4. Contact the testing laboratory.
Reach out to the laboratory that conducted the tests to confirm the results, clarify any uncertainties, and request detailed reports or clarifying information if necessary.

5. Notify the appropriate regulatory body.
Report the failure to the relevant oversight authority promptly – this could be a local health department, environmental agency, or the EPA, depending on your jurisdiction. Make
